properties.name: CAVE MOUNTAIN LAKE DAY USE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Nestled in the Blue Ridge Mountains of Virginia, the Cave Mountain Lake Recreation Area welcomes generations of families who enjoy the rustic beauty and peacefulness of the area. Easy access from I-81, close proximity to historic Lexington, and access to Natural Bridge State Park, make Cave Mountain Lake a perfect travel destination. Cave Mountain Lake also has a wonderful shelter originally built by the CCC, which is available for gatherings, by reservation only (Recreation.gov).

properties.name: STRAIGHT BRANCH
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Straight Branch Trail is a quiet, one-mile doubletrack trail located near Damascus, Virginia in Beartree Campground. This multi-use trail is moderately strenuous and includes a 259 foot climb.

properties.name: RATTLESNAKE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Rattlesnake and Terrapin are the two gravel parking lots available to riders accessing the South Pedlar ATV Trail System. The two parking lots are located less than two miles apart, both along Virginia State Route 130. The South Pedler ATV Trail system is a looping network of 19 miles specifically designed for a recreational ATV rider. Advanced riders will find challenges in the narrow and twisting trails, while others will find trails that are wide and inviting. Visitors to the area enjoy panoramic vistas, spectacular mountain laurel blooms in season, and relief from the hot summer sun under the shady forest canopy.

properties.description: This tiny, stone cabin is available to rent through the Potomic Appalachian Trail Club and is located about 8 miles from Woodstock, VA. Offering 2 double-deck, fold-down bunks and a small wood stove, this cabin is ideal for more adventurous couples. Built for use by national forest rangers circa 1920, the cabin is appropriate for experienced backpackers seeking remote lodging and a difficult hike-in. Access the cabin by a 3.2 mile uphill hike-in on Little Stony Creek Trail. When the trailhead is closed from February through April, park at the Wolf Gap Recreation Area Campground and attempt the 6.7 mile hike-in. This alternate route is not for the faint-hearted or novice hiker.

properties.description: Bubbling Springs is a spring where water emerges from the ground making a pleasant bubbling sound. The area is traditionally used by campers for dispersed camping and visitors coming to see the spring. The Rich Hole Wilderness is nearby. The site does not have access to hiking trails.

properties.name: EVANS TRACT BOATING SITE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.unit: Walter Robinson Canoe Access Point (Evans Tract)
properties.description: Evan's Tract provides access to Cow pasture River and its adjoining fields and woodland. You may hand-launch a small watercraft into the river, but no vehicle access is allowed close to the river. The numerous hay fields in this area support a variety of open country species such as northern bobwhite, indigo bunting, and song sparrow. The neighboring woodland edges hold expected species such as red-bellied and pileated woodpeckers, blue jay, American crow, Carolina wren, northern cardinal, American robin and American goldfinch. The banks of the river should be checked for great blue and green herons as well as the occasional wood duck or belted kingfisher. Damselflies also frequent the river and both powdered dancer and American ruby spot are plentiful. The hay fields along the river attract a variety of butterflies including eastern tiger and spicebush swallowtails, eastern tailed-blue and a confusing array of duskywings and skipper. Notes: - The original access point of this site near the Evans Tract boat ramp is only walkable in winter or early spring due to unmanaged fields and high grasses. - To access it any time of year, use the coordinates below to find the entrance to the Forest Service road running through the tract.

properties.name: NORTH CREEK

properties.description: Located along the edge of North Creek, this campground offers shady campsites and a relaxed atmosphere. Prop your feet up and listen to the stream as it gurgles past, or take advantage of the fishing at your door.

properties.name: SANDY FLATS IRON MOUNTAIN CAMPING AREA
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.unit: SANDY FLATS IRON MOUNTAIN CAMPING AREA
properties.description: The shelter was destroyed by a hurricane. the privy still exists, as does the fire pit.

properties.name: INDIAN DRAFT
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Indian Draft is a river access point along the Jackson and a potential put out point if floating down from Gathright Dam. The rapids at Indian Draft, although not large enough to cause any real danger, add a little excitement to the float down from Gathright Dam. Travelers pass through a corridor flanked by sycamores on both sides and a ceiling of clear blue sky. Each turn provides the observer with a surprise maybe a white-tailed doe and her spotted fawn or perhaps a family of wood ducks with their fluffy young. On closer inspection, the banks hold numerous varieties of wildflowers, including orange and yellow jewelweeds, black-eyed Susan, Asian dayflower and many more.

properties.name: MIDDLE CREEK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This picnic site was built by the CCC. It contains lots of historic and interesting rockwork. This site is no longer maintained regularly.

properties.name: GLENWOOD HORSE TRAIL - HUNTING CREEK TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is a pull-through parking lot adjacent to Hunting Creek Road. The Glenwood Horse Trail is located on the road, in this section. The parking lot is relatively small, but can accommodate 2-3 horse trailers. Within the parking area, park to the right-hand-side of the loop and travel on the left-hand side. The site includes a small bulletin board with area information. Glenwood Horse Trail is immediately out of the parking lot, going both southwest and north east along the Hunting Creek Road.

properties.name: PRIEST A.T. SHELTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is an Appalachain Trail shelter.

properties.name: BLUE SPRINGS GAP CABIN
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Located high on a mountaintop near Camp, VA, Blue Springs Gap Cabin seems to be on top of the world. There are three cozy bedrooms, a kitchen, a living room and a wrap around porch with views of the surrounding mountains. Electricity and flush toilet add comfort to this rustic mountain setting. Bird watching opportunities, hiking trails, and streams for fishing are nearby. Drinking water is not available; be sure to bring your own.

properties.name: GUEST RIVER GORGE TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The Guest River Gorge trail is an accessible out-and-back trail that follows the old Norfolk/Southern railroad bed for 5.9 miles. This flat and paved trail has great views of tall cliffs and waterfalls, and goes through an old railroad tunnel. The original railroad was used for hauling coal mined near the gorge. Though the ties were removed, its trestles and tunnel remain. This trail is popular all year round.

properties.name: SOUTH HOLSTEN/TEAS RD A.T. TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is a small parking lot/trailhead for the A.T. along Teas Road, adjacent to the South Fork of Holsten River.

properties.name: POTTS SLOPE SHOOTING RANGE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This range is for rifle and pistol practice only. The lanes are sheltered from the sun and each one has a shooting bench that accommodates left and right-handed shooters. This range is designed for firing at stationary targets at 25, 50 & 100 yards. Shooters must bring their own paper targets to affix to the wire mesh fence.

properties.name: SMITH BRIDGE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Smith Bridge has a hand launch for access to the river. The stretch of the river at Smith Bridge has a magical feel as it passes between various stages of forest growth from open grass fields to massive ancient sycamores and yellow poplars. The river along this stretch provides homes to water birds such as great blue and green herons, wood duck, and belted kingfisher. Eastern painted turtles populate the fallen logs emerging from the water, while bullfrogs boom from both banks. The edges of the Jackson River are a good area to search for dragon- and damselflies. Dragonflies, such as widow and slaty skimmers, eastern amberwing, common whitetail, common green darner, and damselflies, such as ebony jewelwing, powdered dancer and several bluets and forktails, could occur. A paved path leads to an accessible platform for fishing and viewing the river.

properties.name: BATZELL
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Batzell Boat Launch sits perched on the riverbank. Stunningly clear water laps down the river and the boat ramp allows easy access to the South Fork of the Shenandoah River. Relish the fishing opportunities or soak up some sun on a lazy canoe ride. Watch closely as you don't want to miss an opportunity to spot the Otters frolicking alongside the riverbanks.

properties.name: VA-56 TYE RIVER A.T. TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: VA-56 TYE RIVER A.T. TRAILHEAD (Trailhead)

properties.name: APPLE ORCHARD FALLS NRT TRAIL HEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.unit: Apple Orchard Falls Nrt Trail Head
properties.description: Three trailheads exist for the Apple Orchard Falls National Recreation Trail. One at the top, off the Blue Ridge Parkway; One trailhead in the middle of the trail, off Apple Tree Road; One trailhead at the downhill end, nearest to North Creek Campground and Cornelius Creek Trailhead. The uphill trailhead leaves Sunset Fields at milepost 78.4 on the Blue Ridge Parkway and winds down Apple Orchard Mountain, generally following the headwaters of North Creek. Hikers will follow the coursing stream as it travels down the mountain. The trail pauses at a wooden platform overlooking the waterfalls then travels to a boardwalk at the base of the waterfall. Hikers stopping at the middle trailhead quickly encounter wooden bridges criss-crossing the creek as they progress uphill to the viewing platform. The most downhill trailhead begins in relatively flatter terrain before eventually ascending a steeper grade toward the viewing platform.

properties.name: CHESTNUT KNOB A.T. SHELTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is an Appalachain Trail shelter.

properties.name: COLES POINT BOAT LAUNCH
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Coles Point at Lake Moomaw boasts picnic shelters, two fishing docks, two boat ramps and a swimming beach. Opportunities abound for hiking, photography, nature study, birding and viewing wildlife. Coles Point is perched along the shores of the southern end of Lake Moomaw, providing convenient access to boating, fishing, swimming and relaxing on the beach. The picnic area has an open field for games like Frisbee and soccer. The 1-mile Morris Hill Bike Trail is popular among hikers and bikers. The 3-mile Fortney Loop Trail is open to hiking along a path with several switchbacks.

properties.name: LAKE KEOKEE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Visitors to Lake Keokee Day Use Area enjoy a universally accessible fishing trail and pier.

properties.name: HIGH KNOB CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The High Knob Recreation Area was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) in the late 1930's. This remote and private location offers cooler summer temperatures due to its higher mountain elevation. The area offers a campground and day use and picnic area along a scenic mountain lake. Many of the original CCC structures are still in use here today.

properties.name: DAY CREEK HORSE TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The Day Creek trailhead offers access to Glenwood trail system which stretches northeastward for 68 miles. There is a 25-mile loop that goes over the Blue Ridge into Botetourt County and back via Black Horse Gap and Boblet's Gap. There are also several "out & back" rides available. Trails consist of gravel roads, dirt forest service roads, and wooded trails. Many of these trails are quite rocky and horse shoes are recommended. The trailhead has parking for about 20 horse trailer rigs, a creek for watering horses, and a pit type toilet. This is a popular hunting area during deer season. Overnight camping is discouraged.

properties.name: WAGON ROAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Generally considered a moderately challenging route, it takes an average of 1 h 3 min to complete. This trail is great for hiking and walking, and it's unlikely you'll encounter many other people while exploring. The trail is open year-round and is beautiful to visit anytime. Dogs are welcome, but must be on a leash. Please note the entrance to the trail is at the Little Fort campground. You will see a board with ATV trail info and that is the starting point of the trail.

properties.name: SHERANDO LAKE CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Sherando Lake Recreation Area is known locally as the jewel of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Families enjoy picnicking in this shaded and woody area, while relaxing on the sandy beach of a 25-acre spring-fed lake. Access to multiple trailheads and rustic architecture provide numerous points of interest for families to enjoy. Loop A campsites are generally smaller and suitable for tents or small trailers (not all sites). Loop B and Loop C are larger and include electric pedestals for an added fee (including 110 / 30 / 50 amp outlets). All campsites available by reservation only (Recreation.gov)

properties.name: CLINE'S HACKING
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is a Trailhead for Rocky Run Trail (Forest Trail #426). The Rocky Run ATV/OHV trail (Forest Trail #426) on the North River Ranger District is a loop of approximately 10 miles designated for the recreational, all-terrain vehicle rider. The loop trail is made up of Second Mountain Road (Forest Service Road #502) and Dictum Ridge Road (Forest Service Road #422). Riders will find challenges in the narrow and twisting portion connecting Second Mountain and Dictum Ridge. Other trail sections are wide and inviting.

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Nature viewers enjoy unusual vegetation normally found several hundred miles to the north. Red Spruce and northern hardwoods such as birch, beech, and maple reside here due to frigid soil temperatures. Enjoy the Buck Run and/or the Locust Springs Trails, or hike down one of the trails to Laurel Fork. Visit the adjacent spring which forms the headwaters of Locust Spring Run.

properties.name: ELIZABETH FURNACE CABIN
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: ELIZABETH FURNACE CABIN (Interpretive Site)

properties.name: CHEROKEE FLATS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Designed to accommodate wheelchairs, Cherokee Flats is a streamside, paved trail that provides easy access to fishing holes on Big Stony Creek, a stocked trout stream. A metal ramp permits wheelchair users to experience in-stream fishing. The scenic, 0.5-mile long trail is lined with American holly, rhododendron and wildflowers.

properties.name: PETERS MILL RUN NORTH
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Known as the largest OHV trail system in the state of Virginia, Peters Mill Run and Taskers Gap OHV Trail System provides 36 miles of rugged adventure. Advanced riders will find challenges in steep, rocky and narrow trails, while others can enjoy trails that were once forest roads. All travelers will find mountain vistas, scenic rock outcroppings and the cool shade of deep forest. This trail has opportunities for Jeeps and other 4-wheeled drive vehicles, UTVs, ATVs, motorcycles, and electric mountain bikes.

properties.name: WHITE CEDAR
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Built in 2006, this campground is located on top of Flat Top Mountain. It is perfect for camping with horses; there is plenty of shade and every site has a metal pipe corral. White Cedar's main attraction is its proximity to a 20-mile system of intersecting trails of varied lengths and levels. You can ride directly from your campsite to the Flat Top Trailhead.

properties.name: SETTLERS MUSEUM
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: A visit to the Settlers Museum of Southwest Virginia is like stepping one hundred years into the past. The visitor's center shares the migration story of early European settlers to this region. The restored 19th-century living history farm is a 67-acre open air museum complete with farmhouse and eight original outbuildings and includes a restored 1894 one-room schoolhouse. There are plenty of opportunities for hiking as both the Appalachian Trail and Virginia's Wildlife and Birding Trail run through the property.

Review current VA DWR fishing regulations to ensure that activities are in compliance with catch & release / harvesting rules.

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This recreation site includes a small lake, the original CCC built bathhouse and picnic shelter, and hiking trails. The recreation area was built in the 1930s at the request of the Clifton Forge Chapter of the National Association for the Advancement of Color People (NAACP) and was originally designated for African American visitors during segregation in the United States

properties.name: HELLGATE HORSE TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Provides Access to Glenwood Horse Trail and the Gunter Ridge Hiking Trail. The Gunter Ridge Trail begins off Forest Road #3015 (Gunter Ridge Road) and climbs through a series of switchbacks to the top of Gunter Ridge in the James River Face Wilderness. Continuing along the top of Gunter Ridge and through a gap, the trail is joined by Forest Trail #9, the Belfast Trail, and intersects with Forest Trail #1 - The Appalachian Trail. Horses are allowed on the Glenwood Trail System, but horses are prohibited on the Gunter Ridge Trail.

properties.name: PHILLIPS CREEK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Visitors to Phillips Creek Day Use Area enjoy a beach with creek access and picnicking.

properties.name: TOP DRIVE OVERLOOK

properties.name: KENNEDY PEAK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Kennedy Peak has some of the best vistas in the region. The out and back hike ends with a spectacular 360¿¿ view from the observation tower viewing platform at the summit of Kennedy Peak. The hike itself is reasonably easy. It starts with a gentle incline along the ridge, then climbs more steeply around the western flank of the peak. If you're looking for more of a challenge, add the Stephens Trail to create a 9.2-mile 1,590 ft gain loop hike. Also, before starting out take a moment to check out the paragliding launch area with easterly views of the Shenandoah River and Luray Valley.

properties.name: BLACKSBURG SHOOTING RANGE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Located just outside Blacksburg, this site offers a rifle and pistol range as well as a shotgun and archery range. The rifle and pistol range is designed for firing at stationary paper targets up to 100 meters away. The lanes are sheltered from the sun and each one has a shooting bench that accommodates left and right-handed shooters. Shooters must bring their own targets; cardboard boxes or commercial paper targets work well. The shotgun range is designed for shooting clay targets, which must be provided by shooters. Archery is also permitted at the shotgun range.

properties.name: RAVEN CLIFF
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: From the 200-foot sandstone Raven Cliff to the 1810 iron ore furnace, this recreation area is off the beaten path but worth the effort. With a small primitive campground, picnic area, and large day use area, visitors can spend a few hours or few days. Cripple Creek runs through the picnic area and is popular for fishing, wading, and tubing. Large open fields are great for sports and picnics.

properties.name: NORTH CREEK CABIN

properties.name: TOMAHAWK POND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Come spend the entire day at Tomahawk Pond! For a fun and relaxing angling experience, utilize one of the accessible platforms or treasure a simple picnic with family or friends. Birdwatchers should be on the lookout for the allusive Peregrine Falcon diving for prey.

properties.name: ROARING RUN FURNACE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Roaring Run is a popular get-away for escaping the summer heat. It features shady picnic spots, a native trout stream and a 1.5-mile scenic loop trail that follows Roaring Run Creek to a cascading waterfall. History buffs will enjoy seeing the historic iron furnace that operated prior to the Civil War.

properties.name: BLOWING SPRINGS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Offering both sunny and shaded camping sites, visitors to Blowing Springs Campground will be amazed by the phenomenon for which this site is named. A unique geological feature creates a duct that blows air out of the rocks at a constant 58 degrees, which may feel warm or cool depending on the season. Direct access to trails leading to swimming holes, and a stream stocked with trout are a few of the many reasons to visit this campground.

properties.name: MASSANUTTEN VISITOR CENTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This Site is Permanently Closed

properties.name: STONY FORK CABIN
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Stony Fork is located in a natural forest setting at the foot of Big Walker Mountain and adjacent to the Big Walker Scenic Byway. A short drive from I-77 and I-81, the campground is popular with RVers and tent campers. The East Fork of Stony Fork Creek winds through the campground and provides water play and trout fishing. A one-mile nature trail will take campers through stands of pine and hardwoods, while the campground loop road itself is popular with walkers. For the more experienced hiker, Seven Sisters Trail leads from the campground to the top of Little Walker Mountain and back to the Scenic Byway.

properties.name: WHITE ROCKS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: White Rocks Campground is in a secluded forest setting with cool summertime temperatures and great wildlife watching opportunities. A small creek meanders through several campsites and a nature trail traverses through the woods. Area highlights include Mountain Lake Wilderness, Mountain Lake, Glen Alton Day Use Area, Hanging Rock Raptor Observatory, Potts Rail Trail, Appalachian Trail, and multiple hiking opportunities.

properties.name: PARTNERSHIP A.T. SHELTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

properties.name: HUSSY MOUNTAIN HORSE CAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This primitive campground offers three group camping loops. Each has parking for 4 or 5 vehicles with trailers, wooden picnic tables, fire rings, hitching rails, garbage containers, and direct access to horse trails.

properties.name: CONFEDERATE BREASTWORKS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: A popular scenic viewing area for fall foliage, this winding 0.5-mile interpretive trail meanders along the top of Shenandoah Mountain. Relive the events of April 1862 through the letters of Captain Shepherd Pryor, a member of the 12th Georgia Regiment, to his wife. This is also a popular access point to the gently rolling Shenandoah Mountain Trail and Ramseys Draft Wilderness.

properties.name: WALNUT FLATS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This small, primitive campground is well suited for tent camping but also accommodates small recreation vehicles. It has shaded sites clustered around a grassy opening surrounded by forest. Flat Top Mountain Trail System, the Appalachian Trail, Dismal Creek (a stocked trout stream), and the Falls of Dismal are close by.

properties.name: AUGUSTA SPRINGS WETLANDS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This accessible interpretive trail meanders through various wetland habitats surrounded by hardwood forest which are interspersed with pines. Two large ponds are home to nesting wood duck and are patrolled by resident green and great blue herons. Nesting species include common yellowthroat, red-winged blackbird, blue-gray gnatcatcher, cedar waxwing, American goldfinch, and occasionally, blue-winged warbler. In migration, look for migrants such as wood thrush and scarlet tanager. Sparrow diversity can include resident song sparrow, and in the winter, swamp, white-throated, and American tree sparrows as well. Blooming ironweed, rudbeckia, cardinal flower, Robin's plantain daisies, yarrow, milkweed, and jewelweed line the fields surrounding the ponds and attract ruby-throated hummingbirds. Look for eastern tiger, pipevine, and spicebush swallowtails, Zabulon skipper, Monarch, and many other colorful butterflies. This is an excellent site for those seeking herpetofauna. Black rat snakes can be found slithering from the forest's edge, sometimes basking in the sun along pond banks. Water snakes may be seen swimming in the ponds. Look for frog activity from pickerel and green frogs near the water's edge. Salamanders, such as northern dusky and red-backed, are common as well.

properties.name: BIRCH KNOB
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Visitors to the Birch Knob Observation Tower enjoy views stretching from Virginia, to Kentucky, West Virginia, North Carolina, and Tennessee. The site offers access to the challenging Pine Mountain Trail that meanders along the ridge top between Kentucky and Virginia.

properties.name: ALLEGHENY TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Twelve miles of the Allegheny Trail pass through the James River Ranger District. The Allegheny Trailhead provides an excellent access point for hikers headed for the Laurel Run Trailhead, 15 miles to the north on the Monongahela National Forest. This long distance trail crosses and follows the Eastern Continental Divide in the rugged Allegheny Mountains of West Virginia and Virginia. When complete, it will extend 330 miles from Preston County West Virginia, near the Pennsylvania border, to the Appalachian Trail in Monroe County, West Virginia.

properties.name: POOR FARM
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Hiking and fishing opportunities are abundant at Poor Farm Dispersed Recreation Area. Enjoy hiking trails that meander along the Jackson River, or break out that rod and reel as the trout stocked waters are popular amongst fly and traditional fishermen alike.

properties.name: MOUNT TORRY FURNACE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: MOUNT TORRY FURNACE (Interpretive Site)

properties.name: CRABTREE MEADOWS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: CRABTREE MEADOWS (Trailhead)

properties.name: GREEN COVE STATION
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Green Cove Station was built by the Norfolk and Western Railroad in 1914, and positioned on a stretch of track between Abingdon, Virginia and West Jefferson, North Carolina. The train and the line, became known as the Virginia Creeper because of its slow speed going up and over the mountains. Green Cove was a social center where folks gathered to get their mail, meet the train, and catch up on what was happening with their neighbors. Green Cove is the only original passenger station remaining on what was the Abingdon Branch. Green Cove Station and its contents were given to the USDA Forest Service so that it might be restored and preserved. Today it serves as a gathering and resting spot for thousands of visitors to the Virginia Creeper Trail.

properties.name: POWELLS FORT CAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Powell's Fort Organization Camp is located in Little Fort Valley south of Strasburg, VA. The camp was built as a recreation area for the underprivileged and originally was equipped to accommodate 96 campers and 16 staff members. In 1937, the wavy-edge siding known as waney-edge was required for all buildings in the George Washington National Forest.

properties.name: BRYANT RIDGE A.T. SHELTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is an Appalachain Trail shelter.

properties.name: WHITETOP STATION
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Whitetop Station is a great starting point for an exciting bike ride down the Virginia Creeper Trail. Whitetop Station is a visitor center that shares the story of the local train history and mountain community through displays of historic photos and memorabilia. The current building, constructed in 2000, replaces the original train station that sat atop the highest point on the Abingdon Branch of the Norfolk and Western Rail Lines until it was abandoned in 1977.

properties.name: MOUNTAIN HOUSE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Mountain House Day Use Area provides the primary access to Ramseys Draft Wilderness and an opportunity for a picnic or to stage a hiking adventure. Native trout fishing is available in the adjacent Ramseys Draft stream. The vault toilet is closed December 1st through April 1st. No drinking water is available at this site.

properties.name: SCALES TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Enjoy this 7.6-mile out-and-back trail near Mouth of Wilson, Virginia. Generally considered a moderately challenging route, it takes an average of 3 h 27 min to complete. This is a popular trail for backpacking, camping, and hiking, but you can still enjoy some solitude during quieter times of day. The best times to visit this trail are April through October. Dogs are welcome, but must be on a leash.

properties.name: RICE FIELDS A.T. SHELTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is an Appalachain Trail Shelter

properties.name: MCCLINTIC POINT PRIMITIVE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: McClintic Point at Lake Moomaw sits on the northern end of the lake. Enjoy the easygoing, peaceful vibe of McClintic Point's rustic campground set among scattered trees and open fields. This angler's paradise provides plentiful shoreline fishing and some lakefront campsites. Boating, canoeing, water skiing and fishing are popular activities on the lake.

properties.name: WIND ROCK A.T. TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Wild Rock Trailhead provides access to the Appalachian Trial and Potts Mountain Trail (#55). A short moderate hike uphill will take you to Wind Rock with sweeping views of Rocky Mountains (3300?), Fork Mountain (3645?) and Peter?s Mountain (4000?). Continue on into Mountain Lake Wilderness.

properties.name: THE PINES
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The Pines is a rustic campground in a wooded setting, located adjacent to Barbour's Creek, a stocked trout stream. Most of the campsites are designed for tents, but small recreation vehicles can be accommodated. Jeep enthusiasts can experience some of the most challenging 4-wheeling in Virginia at nearby Potts Mountain Jeep Road.

properties.name: ROCKY RUN TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The is a Trailhead Also known as "Cline's Hacking" for Rocky Run ATV/OHV trail (Forest Trail #426) on the North River Ranger District. It is a loop of approximately 10 miles designated for the recreational, all-terrain vehicle rider. The loop trail is made up of Second Mountain Road (Forest Service Road #502) and Dictum Ridge Road (Forest Service Road #422). Riders will find challenges in the narrow and twisting portion connecting Second Mountain and Dictum Ridge. Other trail sections are wide and inviting.

properties.name: BEARWALLOW
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Parking lot for the Bear Wallow Trailhead located near the Elizabeth Furnace Recreation Area.

properties.name: SIGNAL KNOB
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.unit: Signal Knob Trailhead/Passage Creek Parking Lot
properties.description: Parking lot for the Signal Knob Trailhead.

properties.name: COLES MOUNTAIN GROUP PICNIC SHELTERS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Coles Point Picnic Shelters are tucked in a small opening surrounded by a hardwood forest. Opportunities abound for hiking, photography, nature study, birding and viewing wildlife. Best of all, Coles Point is perched along Moomaw Lake, providing convenient access to boating, fishing, swimming and relaxing on the beach.

properties.name: CAVE MOUNTAIN LAKE CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Nestled in the Blue Ridge Mountains of Virginia, the Cave Mountain Lake Recreation Area welcomes generations of families who enjoy the rustic beauty and peacefulness of the area. Cave Mountain Lake is easily accessed from I-81 and offers close proximity to historic Lexington and access to Natural Bridge State Park.

properties.name: WHISPERING WATERS TRAIL
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is a 0.6-mile loop trail near Troutdale, Virginia. Considered a moderately challenging route, it takes an average of 19 minutes to complete. This trail is great for birding, camping, and hiking, and it's unlikely you'll encounter many other people while exploring. The best times to visit this trail are April through October. Dogs are welcome, but must be on a leash.

properties.name: HARPERS CREEK A.T. SHELTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is an Appalachain Trail shelter.

properties.name: PAUL GERHARD TUSCARORA SHELTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is a primitive Trail Shelter

properties.name: SHERANDO LAKE DAY USE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Sherando Lake Recreation Area is known locally as the jewel of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Families enjoy picnicking in this shaded and woody area, while relaxing on the sandy beach of a 25-acre spring-fed lake. Access to multiple trailheads and rustic architecture provide numerous points of interest for families to enjoy. The Day-Use area also includes Williams Branch Picnic Shelter, which is available for gatherings by reservation only (Recreation.gov).

properties.name: GLEN ALTON
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Glen Alton is a 304-acre property in Giles County that was a working farm until the 1980's. Majestic trees, open pastures and picturesque buildings create a pastoral setting that invites wandering. This day use area features picnic tables, hiking trails, and wildlife watching opportunities. Nearby area highlights include White Rocks Campground, Potts Rail Trail, Big Stony Creek, and Interior Whistle Stop.

properties.name: COLES POINT RECREATION AREA
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Coles Point at Lake Moomaw boasts picnic shelters, two fishing docks, two boat ramps and a swimming beach. Opportunities abound for hiking, photography, nature study, birding and viewing wildlife. Coles Point is perched along the shores of the southern end of Lake Moomaw, providing convenient access to boating, fishing, swimming and relaxing on the beach. The picnic area has an open field for games like Frisbee and soccer. The 1-mile Morris Hill Bike Trail is popular among hikers and bikers. The 3-mile Fortney Loop Trail is open to hiking along a path with several switchbacks.

properties.name: HURRICANE CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Located along a rushing mountain stream under the shade of hemlock and rhododendron, this campground offers a peaceful setting for quiet evenings around the campfire. While only two miles off State Highway 16, the setting feels much more remote. Hikers can walk from their campsite to the Appalachian Trail and many other nearby trails. This site is not recommended for large RVs.

properties.name: ELK GARDEN A.T.
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: With spectacular views and access to multiple trails, Elk Garden is one of the most popular trailheads in the Mount Rogers National Recreation Area. From this location, visitors can access the Appalachian Trail, Virginia Highlands Horse Trail, and the Elk Garden Trail. The trailhead is a short drive from Whitetop Mountain Road, the highest elevation public road in Virginia.

properties.name: WOODSTOCK TWR HANG GLIDING
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Experience the thrill of flying without an airplane! Feel your adrenaline and excitement build as you approach the launch site perched high on the western slope of the Massanutten Mountain. Launch from this challenging site and soar like an eagle while enjoying a bird's eye view of the Shenandoah Valley.

properties.description: This is an AT Trail Shelter in Smyth County Virginia

properties.name: ELIZABETH FURNACE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Elizabeth Furnace Recreation Area offers forested trails, campsites and open grassy picnic areas along the tranquil Passage Creek. Enjoy hiking the Pig Iron and Charcoal interpretive trails and learn how iron was historically mined and smelted. Spend the day fishing from a stocked trout stream, grilling out at a picnic spot, or taking a stroll across the swinging bridge to view the historic cabin.

properties.name: RICH HOLE WILDERNESS - LOWER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Use the Rich Hole WIlderness Trailhead to access the southern portion of NFST #464 Rich Hole Trail

properties.name: LOWMOOR RANGE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This site contains both rifle and handgun shooting ranges, and offers a covered bench for shooting lanes. Shotguns allowed with paper targets only; no skeet or moving target shooting allowed. No automatic weapons.

properties.name: HIGH KNOB TOWER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: On a clear day it's possible to enjoy views of five states from the upper platform of High Knob Tower. Landmarks that can be viewed from the tower are Pine Mountain (Kentucky-Virginia state line), Mount Rogers, Whitetop Mountain, Clinch Mountain, Roan Mountain (Tennessee-North Carolina state line) and the Great Smoky Mountains National Park. Visitors with a smart phone or tablet can access an aid in identifying the prominent landmarks that are visible from High Knob. Go to http://southwestvirginiacsi.wix.com/highknob and click on the get started link. This tool is provided by the University of Virginia-Wise Citizen Science Institute. The observation tower currently standing on High Knob was reconstructed in 2014 and is wheelchair accessible. The previous stone and wood tower was destroyed by an arsonist in 2008. With tremendous support from local communities and the High Knob Enhancement Corporation, funds and grants were secured to rebuild this structure for your enjoyment.

properties.name: PAT JENNINGS VISITOR CENTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The Pat Jennings Visitor Center serves as the headquarters and gateway to the Mount Rogers National Recreation Area. Located only 6 miles from I-81, the visitor center is in a peaceful mountain setting and adjacent to the Appalachian Trail. The center offers interpretative information, maps, clean restrooms and access to the Two Ponds Nature Trail.

properties.name: WILSON CREEK A.T. SHELTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is an Appalachain Trail shelter.

properties.name: STRAIGHT BRANCH IRON MOUNTAIN SHELTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This trail is a pretty steady incline up until you arrive at Straight Branch Shelter. There is a stream near by. Follow the blue blaze trail directly in front of the shelter down the hill. The privy has been torn down. There is also an old fire pit and picnic table.

properties.name: PANDAPAS POND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Pandapas Pond is a pastoral, 8-acre pond located just outside the town of Blacksburg. It sits on the Eastern Continental Divide and is surrounded by a forest of hardwoods and rhododendron. A one-mile, wheelchair accessible trail encircles the pond. A wooden boardwalk separates the pond from a small wetland area that is abundant with dragonflies, turtles, songbirds, and waterfowl. Horses and bicycles are not permitted on the trail around the pond; however they may use the 17-mile Poverty Creek Trail system that can be accessed from the upper parking lot.

properties.name: JENNY KNOB A.T. SHELTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is an Appalachain Trail Shelter

properties.name: TERRAPIN
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Rattlesnake and Terrapin are the two gravel parking lots available to riders accessing the South Pedlar ATV Trail System. The two parking lots are located less than 2 miles apart, both along VA State Highway 130. This looping network of 19 miles is specifically designed for the recreational ATV rider. Advanced riders will find challenges in the narrow and twisting trails, while others will find trails that are wide and inviting. Visitors to the area enjoy panoramic vistas, spectacular mountain laurel blooms in season, and relief from the hot summer sun under the shady forest canopy.

properties.name: HIGH KNOB MULTIUSE

properties.name: GOODS LANDING BOATING SITE (MOODY)
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Goods Landing has a concrete boat ramp on river left at the end of Riverwater Road off of Page Valley Road. This is an excellent and relatively secluded access point for a variety of water recreation. This ramp gives you access to a nice relatively deep pool. Goods Landing is about 2 miles downstream from Fosters Landing, and 3.3 miles upstream from Seekford Landing, all on river left.

properties.name: BARK CAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The day use area and trails are open all year. The campground is open from the 3rd Saturday in May to the last Saturday in September. The site features a 45-acre lake that is regularly stocked with rainbow trout. A three-mile shoreline trail circles the lake, offering outstanding views. The Kitchen Rock Trail leads to an intersting rock formation. Other features include an open-air amphitheater, universally accessible fishing piers, a boat ramp, courtesy dock, and picnicking facilities.

properties.name: JAMES RIVER FOOTBRIDGE- AT
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The James River Foot Bridge carries the Appalachian Trail over the James River in Snowden, Virginia, approximately 20 miles northwest of Lynchburg. The bridge was built on the piers of a demolished CSX bridge that had been replaced with a longer trestle just east of the original bridge, providing a straighter course for freight traffic. Trains pass by frequently against the scenic backdrop of rolling hills and refreshing water below. When opened in 2000, the James River Foot Bridge eliminated a dangerous crossing of the James River that mixed hikers with vehicular traffic on U.S. Route 501. A curious note: While this is indeed a footbridge, its name actually refers to Bill Foot, an Appalachian Trail enthusiast who spearheaded the conversion of the bridge into its present use. Parking and Trail Access Parking for the James River Foot Bridge and Appalachian Trail is available on the north side of the James River in Snowden, Virginia. Swimming and Jumping from the James River Foot Bridge is Prohibited.

properties.name: THUNDER HILL A.T. SHELTER

properties.name: WOODSTOCK TOWER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Don't miss the opportunity to take in the grand views from the Woodstock Tower! In 1935, the historical structure was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps with the material provided by the Woodstock Chamber of Commerce. The tower offers views of the beautiful Seven Bends in the North Fork of the Shenandoah River.

properties.name: TRIMPI A.T. SHELTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The Trimpi Shelter is a stone shelter built in 1975 and located in Southern Virginia just north of Troutville. This shelter is maintained by the Mt. Rogers Appalachian Trail Club.

properties.name: CRAIG CREEK A.T. PARKING
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This provides access to the #5006 Craig Creek Trail inside the Craig Creek Recreation Area

properties.name: TODD LAKE CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Visitors to Todd Lake Recreation Area enjoy a historic campground complete with a wheelchair accessible beach. There is a children's playground, plenty of open fields, grills, and picnic tables making this location an ideal place to spend a relaxing summer afternoon. Explore nearby trails popular among mountain biking, backpacking, and hiking enthusiasts. The Campground boasts 18 moderately sized campsites, two of which are accessible, hot showers and water at community hydrants.

properties.name: WYTHE SHOOTING RANGE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This range includes a total of 10 benches and shooting lanes. Five are dedicated pistol lanes (25 yards only), three are dedicated rifle lanes (100 yards) and the final two are intermediate lanes available to both. The pistol (25 yard) lanes can have targets set at seven, 10, 15 and 25 yards. The rifle (100 yard) lanes can have targets set at 25, 50 and 100 yards. The intermediate lanes can have targets set at seven, 10, 15, 25, 50 and 100 yards.

properties.name: BEALERS FERRY
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Off the beaten path and well worth the trip, Bealers' Ferry Pond is a refreshing outdoor retreat. Appreciate a quality angling experience that allows one to fish for largemouth bass, bluegill, and channel catfish. Utilize the wheelchair accessible trail that leads to the pier with picturesque views overlooking the attractive scenery. Watch as ducks, geese, and Great Blue Herons skim the waters, and frogs croak loudly along the riverbanks.

properties.name: RACCOON BRANCH
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Only 11 miles from I-81 via State Route 16, this beautiful little campground is nestled at the base of Dickey Knob and adjacent to Raccoon Branch Wilderness. Raccoon Branch campground offers scenic mountain views, hiking from your campsite, and cold mountain streams. Popular for trout fishing, summer vacations, and fall foliage viewing.

properties.name: COLLINS COVE (RAVEN CLIFF) HORSE CAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This primitive campground with easy access to the Virginia Highlands Horse Trail consists of two large grassy fields with wooden picnic tables, fire rings, and hitching rails. Horse owners need to have a current negative Coggins test certificate for any horse that they take to a public place for recreational use in Virginia.

properties.name: BEARWALLOW HORSE TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Beginning at the small parking area at Blackhorse Gap, the trail heads northeast, paralleling the Blue Ridge Parkway to Bearwallow Gap. For those looking for a short day hike, the Appalachian Trail is accessible at several points through this stretch. (However, horses are prohibited anywhere on the Appalachian National Scenic Trail.) A series of developed parking areas serve as junctions for the trail, as well as picturesque overlooks for passing vehicles. Harvey's Knob, a particularly popular overlook for birding, lies a few miles north on the trail.

properties.name: JENKINS  AT TRAILHEAD PARKING
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: JENKINS AT TRAILHEAD PARKING (Trailhead)

properties.name: NATIONAL CHILDRENS FOREST
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The Eastern National Children's Forest is a unique site offering an easy hike for children and others who want an outdoor experience without an arduous and challenging hike. In 1971 a wildfire burned 1,176 acres on Potts Mountain which is about 22 miles south of the City of Covington. In 1972, over 1,000 children converged on the site from surrounding states and planted pine trees on the site. Since the planting a diverse forest ecology has developed with species of various soft and hardwoods. A monument remains with the names of the participating children and a time capsule which is to be opened in the year 2072.

properties.name: BUZZARD ROCK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Park at this trailhead to hike Buzzard Rock Trail #404 to Buzzard Rock Do not park on VA 619 Mountian Road; you will be ticketed and towed.

properties.name: PEARIS CEMETARY & AT
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Appalachian Trail access in Pearisburg, VA

properties.name: FENWICK MINES
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Visitors to Fenwick Mines will find trails to hike, ponds to fish, and a picnic shelter complete with horseshoe pit. A one-mile, wheelchair accessible trail will lead you through wetland, stream, and forest habitats providing lots of opportunities to see wildlife.

properties.name: LOCHER TRACT
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The Locher Tract is a 378-acre area that was once the Locher family farm, where they mined shale to sell to the brick-making plant across the river in Glasgow. Birdwatchers will enjoy a variety of common and unusual species including Pileated Woodpecker, American Goldfinch, Prothonotary and Prairie Warbler. Deer, turkey, rabbits, and other small game thrive in the woods and grassy areas, while the pond is home to waterfowl and beaver. The Locher Tract also serves as one trailhead for the Balcony Falls Trail, accessing the James River Face Wilderness.

properties.name: SUGAR HOLLOW POND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: No information

properties.name: CASCADES
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Cascades Day Use Area is one of the most popular outdoor recreation spots in southwest Virginia, featuring the scenic 66-foot Cascade Falls, a dramatic waterfall located two miles from the parking area. The site includes shady picnic spots, a native trout stream, and a 4-mile scenic loop trail.

properties.name: HIDDEN VALLEY CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: With vast fields of wildflowers that attract countless butterflies, birds, and other wildlife, the Hidden Valley Recreation Area is appropriately named due to its secluded and hidden feeling. Drawing visitors for hundreds of years, the valley is a historic location with an antebellum-era mansion which is now run as a Bed and Breakfast. Camping is available at the campground. Stocked with trout, the Jackson River flows through the valley, and movie buffs will recognize the area as the setting for the movie Somersby.

properties.name: PATTERSON MOUNTAIN ATV
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: George Washington & Jefferson National Forests Supervisor, Maureen Hyzer issued a temporary, emergency closure of the 16-mile Patterson Mountain ATV Trail System, located in Botetourt County, Virginia. The U.S. Forest Service recently completed water quality monitoring and found this motorized trail system is adversely affecting soils, resulting in a high level of sedimentation in adjacent streams. The current condition of the trails is not compliant with standards found in the Jefferson National Forest Plan.

properties.name: HIGHLAND SCENIC BYWAY CORRIDOR COMPOSITE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The Highlands Scenic Drive is a 19 mile loop between Clifton Forge in Alleghany County and Interstate 64 at Lexington. The scenic drive is a must-see experience for all visiting Virginia's Western Highlands and makes the outdoors and nature accessible even to those who would rather not hike into a wilderness area.

properties.name: HANGING ROCK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Hanging Rock is named for the large rock outcrop formed millions of years ago from seismic activity along the Hunters Valley fault. Fossils are visible in the large boulders strewn across Little Stony Creek. The Hanging Rock Day Use Area also serves as the eastern trailhead for the Little Stony National Recreation Trail.

properties.name: ELKHORN LAKE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This day use area is a popular non-motorized boating and fishing area with a wheelchair accessible pier. Elkhorn Day Use Area serves as a municipal watershed for Staunton, VA.

properties.name: MORRIS HILL GROUP CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Morris Hill at Lake Moomaw offers a peaceful, rustic campground. The campground offers scenic views from its perch on a ridge above the southern end of Lake Moomaw. Located just a half-mile from the lakeshore, this campground provides easy access to sandy swim beaches, a fishing pier, boat ramp, and hiking and biking trails. Hikers enjoy the nearby Morris Hill Bike Trail and Fortney Loop Trail.

properties.name: CAMP ROOSEVELT
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Camp Roosevelt Campground is the site of the first Civilian Conservation Corps Camp in the Nation. Follow the path through the CCC camp and view the foundations where the actual buildings once stood. Proud and lofty oak trees create the perfect atmosphere for enjoying a simple picnic or camping out with friends or family.

properties.name: PIG IRON TRAIL
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Pig Iron Interpretive is a 1,552 ft singletrack trail located near Strasburg Virginia @ Elizabeth Furnace Day Use Area that teaches about how iron was historically mined and smelted.

properties.name: TASKERS GAP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Known as the largest OHV trail system in the state of Virginia, Peters Mill Run and Taskers Gap OHV Trail System provides 36 miles of rugged adventure. Advanced riders will find challenges in steep, rocky and narrow trails, while others can enjoy trails that were once forest roads. All travelers will find mountain vistas, scenic rock outcroppings and the cool shade of deep forest. This trail has opportunities for Jeeps and other 4-wheeled drive vehicles, UTVs, ATVs, motorcycles, and electric mountain bikes.

properties.name: BOLAR MOUNTAIN GROUP PICNIC SHELTER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Bolar Mountain Recreation Area at Lake Moomaw offers visitors a fun getaway on Lake Moomaw. The area provides opportunities for plenty of activities, including camping, boating, fishing and hiking, as well as volleyball and a playground. The recreation area sits on the northern end of Lake Moomaw, a manmade lake covering 2,530 acres along the Jackson River. The lake's average depth is 80 feet and it has 43 miles of wooded shoreline. Bolar Mountain boasts 11 miles of hiking trails that lead to two impressive scenic overlooks: Islands Overlook Spur and Grouse Point Overlook.

properties.name: DRAGON'S TOOTH TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Dragons Tooth is a spectacular rock formation located on top of Cove Mountain. The 2.3 mile trail leading to Dragons Tooth is a gradual uphill climb for the first mile until it joins the Appalachian Trail and begins to climb steeply. This part of the hike is strenuous and requires rock scrambling near the top. You'll need your hands and feet to climb the last rocky sections to reach "The Tooth," a 35-foot rock spire. At the top, you'll be rewarded with a jumble of rugged rock outcroppings and panoramic views. Allow plenty of time and daylight to do this challenging hike. Many hikers will take six hours or more to complete the hike.

properties.name: GREEN COVE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Green Cove Station was built by the Norfolk and Western Railroad in 1914, and positioned on a stretch of track between Abingdon, Virginia and West Jefferson, North Carolina. The train and the line, became known as the Virginia Creeper because of its slow speed going up and over the mountains. Green Cove was a social center where folks gathered to get their mail, meet the train, and catch up on what was happening with their neighbors. Green Cove is the only original passenger station remaining on what was the Abingdon Branch. Green Cove Station and its contents were placed in the care of the USDA Forest Service so that it might be restored and preserved. Today it serves as a gathering and resting spot for thousands of visitors to the Virginia Creeper Trail.

properties.name: STEEL BRIDGE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Enjoy splashing or fishing in the cool water of Potts Creek, a stocked trout stream adjacent to this rustic campground and day use area. The campground has three unpaved and well-shaded campsites situated along a single dirt road that parallels the creek. A parking area is available for day-use visitors. Historic Paint Bank, Virginia is a scenic three mile drive from here.

properties.name: FOX CREEK HORSE CAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: For horseback riders, this campground offers unparalleled access to the most scenic trail riding in our region. Ride from your campsite to enjoy a spectacular day of riding in the Mount Rogers High Country that is arguably the best in the eastern U.S. Horse owners need to have a current negative Coggins test certificate for any horse that they take to a public place for recreational use in Virginia.

properties.name: BOLEY FIELDS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This large, open field is good for groups that wish to picnic and tent camp together but require few amenities. It is located at the base of Brush Mountain and the surrounding forest provides shade. Poverty Creek flows adjacent to the field's picnic area. Hikers and mountain bikers can easily access the 17-mile Poverty Creek Trail System from Boley Field. Site is limited to 25 people and 10 vehicles.

properties.description: The Cherry Tree Shelter was constructed right around the time that the AT moved away from its original route along Iron Mountain to the present route that passes through the Grayson Highlands. Some hikers who still followed the old route of the trail into the late 1950s reported staying at this shelter -- the only one west of the New River along the old trail route.

properties.name: MINNIE BALL HILL
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Union Soldiers traveling along Sal Sulfur Tunrpike (part of which is the modern Mountain Lake Road) in 1864 abandoned supplies at this location in order to get over the mountain and back home to West Virginia.

properties.description: Caldwell Fields offers two large, open fields for group camping, Milton and George Fields, ideal for campers who require few amenities. A third field is available at the site for day-use only. The day use field is currently designated as a First Amendment Gathering Site.

properties.name: EDINBURG GAP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Known as the largest OHV trail system in the state of Virginia, Peters Mill Run and Taskers Gap OHV Trail System provides 36 miles of rugged adventure. Advanced riders will find challenges in steep, rocky and narrow trails, while others can enjoy trails that were once forest roads. All travelers will find mountain vistas, scenic rock outcroppings and the cool shade of deep forest. This trail has opportunities for Jeeps and other 4-wheeled drive vehicles, UTVs, ATVs, motorcycles, and electric mountain bikes.

properties.name: EDITH GAP HANG GLIDING
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Experience the thrill of flying without an airplane! Feel your adrenaline and excitement build as you approach the launch site perched high on the southeastern slope of the Massanutten Mountain Ridge in Luray, Virginia. Launch from this steep slope and soar like an eagle while enjoying a bird's eye view of Page County, South Fork River, and the Shenandoah Valley.

properties.name: FLAT TOP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The Flat Top Trail Parking Area on the Blue Ridge Parkway is the location for the northern end of the Flat Top Trail, which runs 4.4 miles from here to the Peaks of Otter Campground. Along the way it ascends to the top of Flat Top Mountain, one of three mountains in the area. The trail climbs 2,400 feet from the Parkway to the peak (elevation 4,004). A short spur trail, the Cross Rock Trail (.2 mile round trip), branches off the Flat Rock Trail on the hike up the mountain. You can also access the Fallingwater Cascades Trail from here. A 200-foot connector trail is located on the other side of the Blue Ridge Parkway. The Fallingwater Cascades Trail is a very popular loop hike, and it has its own parking area less than a half mile to the north.

properties.name: FOX CREEK A.T.
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This small and very busy trailhead has limited parking near the Fox Creek Horse Campground and provides access to the Appalachian Trail.

properties.name: INTERIOR WHISTLESTOP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The Interior Whistle Stop is a shady picnic area along Big Stony Creek featuring picnic tables, grassy areas, and a child-sized wooden train playground. Big Stony Creek is a stocked trout stream.

properties.name: SKULLS GAP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Skull Gap has seven picnic units with tables, grills and a parking spur, the one-mile Skulls Gap Trail is rated moderate as it travels along old Virginia State Route 600. Skulls Gap Trail is available for hiking, biking and horseback riding.

properties.name: HIGH KNOB DAY USE AREA

properties.name: ELIZABETH FURNACE FAMILY PICNIC
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Elizabeth Furnace Recreation Area offers forested trails, campsites and open grassy picnic areas along the tranquil Passage Creek. Enjoy hiking the Pig Iron and Charcoal interpretive trails and learn how iron was historically mined and smelted. Spend the day fishing from a stocked trout stream, grilling out at a picnic spot, or taking a stroll across the swinging bridge to view the historic cabin.

properties.name: CRAIG CREEK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Large grassy fields are the first things you'll see when you enter Craig Creek Day Use Area, but the creek itself is the real highlight. Generations of families have enjoyed the swimming hole here and it's still a great place to escape the heat of summer. Canoeists can use the area as a put-in or take-out point and enjoy an easy paddle on the warm waters of Craig Creek. A grassy field inside the day use area may be reserved for group camping

properties.name: BEARTREE CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is a popular recreation area beside the scenic Beartree Lake complete with campsites, a picnic area, and nearby trails. Campsites are popular with tent campers since there are no hookups, but RVs are welcome and easily accommodated. There are 35 camping units in Chipmunk Circle and 35 camping units in Beaver Flats that are available for tents and RVs. Some sites are available for reservations while others are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Each unit has a parking spur, lantern post, fire grill and picnic table. Bathhouses with toilets, warm showers, sinks, and drinking water are provided. Four walk-in tent clusters and 4 paved RV clusters are available in the Group Loop for reservation. A trailer waste disposal station is located near the campground's exit. Recreation vehicles up to 40 feet can be accommodated in some units.

properties.description: This is a former Appalachian Trail Shelter which has been moved to the vicinity of North Creek Campground / Jennings Creek area. Walk ~200 yards behind a closed gate to access the camping area.

properties.name: PETTICOAT JUNCTION
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Petticoat Junction is a small hand launch for water craft and the last pull out before floating down into Covington. This area holds a variety of habitats from open fields to woodland. These surroundings support anticipated birds such as indigo buntings and song sparrows. Along forest edges these birds can be heard singing from prominent points and popping out of denser patches of scrub and grass. The woods ring with the familiar calls of Carolina wren, northern cardinal and northern flicker, while the river hosts great blue and green herons, wood duck and belted kingfisher. Butterflies such as eastern tiger swallowtail and red-spotted purple float between cardinal flowers and black-eyed Susan's. The glittering ebony jewelwing sticks to shady sections along the stream, often sharing their perch with eastern painted turtles.

properties.name: PINE SWAMP A.T. TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Trailhead that gives access to Peters Mountain Wilderness and the A.T. from Virginia Route 635.

properties.name: OLD VIRGINIA GROUP HORSE CAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This campground is a primitive horse camp with room for 6 to 15 horse trailers, depending on the size. It offers easy access to the Virginia Highlands Horse Trail with its connections to the Iron Mountain Trail. From the Iron Mountain Trail, riders can also access the New River Trail.

properties.name: WAR SPUR TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: War Spur Loop is an easy trail through the Mountain Lake Wilderness that treats hikers to a wide variety of plant life and an outstanding view. Most hikers travel the loop counter-clockwise, following the Salt Pond Mountain ridge to the overlook. In spring, you'll see an array of wildflowers, rhododendron blooms, and flame azaleas. In fall, you'll be surrounded by the colorful foliage and giant ferns. The overlook offers views of the Mountain Lake Wilderness, Johns Creek Mountain, and the valley below. On the return hike to the trailhead, you will walk through a rhododendron thicket and pass a number of large spruce, oak, and hemlock. Shortly before arriving at the trailhead, the War Branch Connector Trail heads north linking War Spur Loop to the Appalachian Trail and then on to Wind Rock overlook.

properties.name: UNAKA
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The Unaka trail is an interpretive nature trail located at Comers Rock.

properties.name: BOLAR MOUNTAIN VOLUNTEER VILLAGE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is a site for Volunteers on the James River and Warm Springs District to base operations out of. The sites have water and electric and there is place to do laundry and shower.

properties.name: DEVIL'S FORK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Devil?s Fork is a 6.9 mile loop trail. The trail leads to a popular geologic feature known as the Devil?s Bathtub. The lower portion of the trail follows a stream, Devils Fork, and meanders by numerous small waterfalls. This trail is rugged, with uneven footing, and more than ten stream crossings with no bridges. Portions of the trail are steep and slippery. Visitors should be prepared for a strenuous hike and should plan accordingly. This trail is very popular, and parking is limited. The access road to the small trailhead may require a high clearance vehicle. Additional parking is available at a nearby county park.

properties.name: MASSANUTTEN STORYBOOK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Stroll along this 0.5 mile interpretive trail that leads to a spectacular view overlooking the Blue Ridge Mountains and Page Valley. Learn from the interpretive signs how the Massanutten Mountains were formed. This is the perfect outdoor retreat to reconnect with nature as you utilize our story-telling rock rings for reading a book, writing in a journal, sharing tales with friends, or just taking a moment to listen to the sounds of nature. Trail is wheelchair accessible.

properties.name: WHITETOP MOUNTAIN
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Whitetop Mountain is the second highest mountain in Virginia and offers the highest public road in the state which leads to a summit of 5525 feet. The summit provides panoramic views of three states on clear days and is known for the unique flora and fauna. Of historic interest, the site was the location for the annual Whitetop Folk Festival from 1932 to 1939.

properties.name: DISCOVERY WAY
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Come explore this .25 mile paved interpretive trail as you enjoy the magic of the surrounding forest. Discover a toothbrush tree, rock with living skin, and leaves in the shape of a mitten! Treasure the sounds of birds chirping and wind moving through the trees overhead. Witness an old millstone that was used to ground grain for hot bread and delicious buckwheat pancakes.

properties.name: JOHNSON SPRINGS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Johnson Springs provides access to a serene mirror calm stretch of the Jackson River. Massive sycamores stretch out over the river along the bank, hosting chickadee and titmouse flocks as they travel the river in search of food. These assemblies can also include less common species such as worm-eating warbler and white-eyed vireo. The scrubby fields next to the stream support open country species such as indigo bunting, American goldfinch, and song sparrow. Watch along the bank for congregations of butterflies concentrated in moist areas of sand. These include eastern tiger and spicebush swallowtails, eastern tailed-blue and pearl crescent. The shadier edges of the river also host the glittering ebony jewelwing dragonfly. Notes: The US Army Corps of Engineers releases water from Gathright Dam on a regular basis, but also as needed. Check the COE's website before heading out.
