properties.name: LIONS TALE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Located on Crisman Hollow Road, the Lions Tail National Recreation Trail is a .5 mile wheelchair accessible trail, with interpretive signage emphasizing the use of senses.

properties.name: CREEK JUNCTION TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: A narrow gravel road provides visitors access to fishing in Whitetop Laurel Creek, hiking and biking access to the Virginia Creeper Trail, and views from underneath the longest trestle on the Virginia Creeper Trail. An accessible fishing trail has piers constructed over the creek for wheelchair access. While easily accessed from State Route 58, the gravel road is not recommended for trailers, RVs, or wide loads.

properties.name: CRABTREE FALLS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This moderate 2.7 mile trail wanders through the mountainside offering scenic views of 5 major cascades falling a total distance of 1,200 feet. Overlooks allow hikers to enjoy the beauty of the valley. The first waterfall overlook is a universally accessible trail, and is only a short distance along a paved trail. Follow the gravel trail uphill around numerous switchbacks for additional close views of the cascading waterfall. A large observation deck at the top of the waterfall offers wonderful views of the valley below.

properties.name: STONY FORK CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Stony Fork is located in a natural forest setting at the foot of Big Walker Mountain and adjacent to the Big Walker Scenic Byway. A short drive from I-77 and I-81, the campground is popular with RVers and tent campers. The East Fork of Stony Fork Creek winds through the campground and provides water play and trout fishing. A one-mile nature trail will take campers through stands of pine and hardwoods, while the campground loop road itself is popular with walkers. For the more experienced hiker, Seven Sisters Trail leads from the campground to the top of Little Walker Mountain and back to the Scenic Byway.

properties.name: SHERANDO LAKE GROUP CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Sherando Lake Recreation Area is known locally as the jewel of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Families enjoy picnicking in this shaded and woody area, while relaxing on the sandy beach of a 25-acre spring-fed lake. Access to multiple trailheads and rustic architecture provide numerous points of interest for families to enjoy. The Group Camping area is designated for tent camping only. There are five distinct campsites suitable for up to 15 campers each. When all five campsites are occupied by a single group, the Group Size Limit is 75 people. A large grassy common space in the middle of the Group Camp Area is a great place to gather or organize pick up ball games.

properties.name: FLATWOODS PICNIC
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Flatwoods Group Picnic area is a secluded site surrounded by forest and offers an excellent setting for group events. Open lawn areas are adjacent to the picnic area. Hiking trails are available within easy driving distance, including Guest River Gorge, Chief Benges Scout, and Little Stony Falls Trails. Facilities include a paved parking lot, picnic shelter and restroom facilities. The picnic shelter has sinks with running water, electrical outlets, and a large built-in charcoal grill. The picnic shelter is designed to be used for food preparation and as a serving area. Picnic tables are adjacent to the shelter but are outside and exposed to the weather.

properties.name: AT/SARTAIN TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Check out this 9.3-mile out-and-back trail near Newport, Virginia. Generally considered a moderately challenging route, it takes an average of 4 h 1 min to complete. This trail is great for hiking and running, and it's unlikely you'll encounter many other people while exploring. Dogs are welcome and may be off-leash in some areas. This trailhead can also be called John's Creek Valley Trailhead by some.

properties.name: LITTLE FORT
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Little Fort is a minimally developed recreation area located near a meadow that was once a rest stop for a stagecoach line. Enjoy the thrill of riding the largest OHV system in the state of Virginia with easy access right from the campground to the Peters Mill Run/Taskers Gap OHV trail system.

properties.name: HOPPER CREEK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Hopper Creek Group Campground offers a shaded and rustic atmosphere for group tent camping with an open area for activities and a large campfire ring for evening gatherings. Because only one group can reserve the area at a time, it offers a great opportunity for privacy and solitude. No trailers, pop-ups, or RV's. Tent camping only. Group Size is limited to 50 people.

properties.description: This is an Appalachain Trail Shelter

properties.name: HENLEY HOLLOW TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This trailhead is just off US21 at the start of Henley Hollow Trail. From there, it's a difficult but manageable, narrow singletrack climb up to Virginia Highlands Horse Trail (VHHT) #337: Divide Trail to US21. A number of root jumps and sharp turns will also seek to impede your progress. If you're using this as a base for the Horse Heaven loop, your reward for this climb is the opportunity to ride it downhill at the end.

properties.name: EDINBURG GAP OHV
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Known as the largest OHV trail system in the state of Virginia, Peters Mill Run and Taskers Gap OHV Trail System provides 36 miles of rugged adventure. Advanced riders will find challenges in steep, rocky and narrow trails, while others can enjoy trails that were once forest roads. All travelers will find mountain vistas, scenic rock outcroppings and the cool shade of deep forest. This trail has opportunities for Jeeps and other 4-wheeled drive vehicles, UTVs, ATVs, motorcycles, and electric mountain bikes.

properties.name: GRINDSTONE FAMILY CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: At 3,800 feet in elevation, this campground offers an escape from summer's heat and excellent birding opportunities. The campground provides access to the Mount Rogers Trail which goes to the top of Mount Rogers. Other features includes a creek, playground and the Whispering Waters Nature Trail.

properties.name: COMERS ROCK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This small primitive campground and historic picnic area are located on top of Iron Mountain at 3800 feet. The log picnic shelter with large stone fireplace was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps. Within walking distance of the campground are long distance hikes in Little Dry Run Wilderness, 360 degree views from Comers Rock Overlook and former fire tower, and the Unaka Nature Trail. Less than two miles away is Hale Lake for fishing, hiking, and canoeing.

properties.name: NORTH RIVER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This open area campground was originally constructed as a CCC camp. Evidence of the original sites and logging trails still remain today. North River Gorge is a popular hiking, biking, and fishing area with a swinging bridge spanning the North River. Close proximity to Wild Oak National Recreation Trail, Stanton Dam Day Use Area and Elkhorn Lake provide multiple recreational options that are easily accessible within a few miles. The campground is made up of nine campsites, none of which are accessible, and each contain a picnic table, fire ring, and lantern post

properties.name: ELIZABETH FURNACE GROUP CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Elizabeth Furnace Recreation Area offers forested trails, campsites and open grassy picnic areas along the tranquil Passage Creek. Enjoy hiking the Pig Iron and Charcoal Interpretive trails and learn how iron was historically mined and smelted. Spend the day fishing from a stocked trout stream, grilling out at a picnic spot, or taking a stroll across the swinging bridge to view the historic cabin.

properties.name: SUNRISE CABIN
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This beautiful two story home of more that 2,500 square feet features four bedrooms and two baths. It has electricity and a large kitchen with refrigerator, stove, and sink. There are beautiful wooden floors throughout and great views from the front porch. Outside there is a small patio with a grill. The cabin is close to the New River Trail.

properties.name: DAVIS FARM CAMPSITE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Davis Farm Campsite is .5 miles off the A.T. down a steep switchback. It is on a steep slope that has been flattened for a couple of tents. Davis Farm Campsite is a great view of the valley below, and looks west for a great sunset. There might also be the sound of cows mooing in the valley below

properties.name: CAVE SPRINGS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Cave Springs Recreation Area is situated within the picturesque farming community of Olinger Gap. Highlights of this recreation area include a campground, small spring-fed pond, access to Stone Mountain Trail and Wilderness, and a short hike to an overlook of the Olinger Gap Community.

properties.name: CANE PATCH
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Cane Patch Campground is within walking distance of Phillips Creek Day Use Area. The campground has 35 campsites, 7 of which have electric hookups.

properties.name: GREENWOOD POINT PRIMITIVE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Greenwood Point Campground at Lake Moomaw offers the solitude of an isolated and remote location. With no road access, the adventure is just getting there! Strap on that pack and take a hike, paddle, or canoe directly to the shores of the campground. Wooded campsites encircle an open and grassy common area, and lakeside views make this a popular private and quiet camping destination.

properties.name: MORRIS HILL
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Morris Hill at Lake Moomaw offers a peaceful, rustic campground. The campground offers scenic views from its perch on a ridge above the southern end of Lake Moomaw. Located just a half-mile from the lakeshore, this campground provides easy access to sandy swim beaches, a fishing pier, boat ramp, and hiking and biking trails. Hikers enjoy the nearby Morris Hill Bike Trail and Fortney Loop Trail.

properties.name: LOST WOMAN
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Use Cobbler Mountain Trailhead to access trails #612 - Lost Woman (Lower Loop), #612A - River Loop, and #613 - Lost Woman (Upper Loop); connects to #611.1 - Cobbler Mountain Access and #611 - Cobbler Mountain.

properties.name: YELLOW BRANCH
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Utilize the Yellow Branch Trailhead to access NFST #310 Yellow Branch Trail; trail continues to NFST #317 Bournes Branch in 3 miles and intersects with NFST #301 Iron Mountain Trail in approximately 4.5 miles.

properties.name: TODD LAKE BEACH & PICNIC SITE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Visitors to Todd Lake Recreation Area enjoy a historic campground complete with a wheelchair accessible beach. There is a children's playground, plenty of open fields, grills, and picnic tables making this location an ideal place to spend a relaxing summer afternoon. Explore nearby trails popular among mountain biking, backpacking, and hiking enthusiasts.

properties.name: SHAWS FORK HORSE CAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This equestrian campground, which has 5 campsites, provides access to trailheads and is popular among hunters. This site is also near the historic Civil War battlefield in McDowell, VA. This campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis.

properties.name: SAINT MARYS WILDERNESS TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The Saint Mary?s Trail follows the picturesque Saint Mary?s River, a native trout stream in a designated wilderness area. A moderate 4.4-mile out-and-back hike leads to the popular Saint Mary?s waterfall by connecting with the Saint Mary?s Gorge trail (Forest Trail #500B). Portions of the trail are located on old railroad grades and mining roads that follow the stream into the gorge. There are several deep pools in the stream along the route, including at the base of the falls. Be prepared to get your feet wet. There are five stream crossings to reach the falls. Wear sturdy boots for the rocky trail which travels through a gorge. The entire hike is within the Saint Mary?s Wilderness Area.

properties.name: WALTON TRACT CANOE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: The Walton Tract Canoe Access Point is located on a former dairy farm along the Cow pasture River. In addition to canoeing, there are opportunities for fishing and hiking. Follow the hiking signs for access to the Beards Mountain Trail which can be reached by crossing a swinging bridge.

properties.name: RICH HOLE WILDERNESS - UPPER
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Use the Rich Hole WIlderness Trailhead to access the northern portion of NFST #464 Rich Hole Trail

properties.name: HONE QUARRY CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Hone Quarry Campground is within one mile of Hone Quarry Reservoir. Nearby trailheads lead to popular rock climbing areas. Highlights of the campground include a picturesque stream, a hike to a nearby 15-foot waterfall and an adjacent group picnic shelter that is non-fee and is available first-come first-served.

properties.name: NORTH RIVER (STAUNTON DAM DAY USE AREA)
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: A historic masonry dam, constructed in the 1920s, and reservoir are highlights of this picnic area. Water flows from the dam through a tunnel beneath Lookout Mountain, serving as the primary water supply for the city of Staunton. The reservoir offers fishing opportunities.

properties.name: APPLE ORCHARD FALLS & APPLE TREE ROAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.unit: Apple Orchard Falls & Apple Tree Road Trailhead
properties.description: The Apple Tree Road (FSR #3034) Trailhead serves #17B Apple Orchard Falls Connector Trail Four trailheads exist for the Apple Orchard Falls National Recreation Trail: one at the top, off the Blue Ridge Parkway; two trailheads in the middle of the trail, off Apple Tree Road (FSR3034) and Parkers Gap Road (812) respectively; and one trailhead at the downhill end, at the end of North Creek Road (FSR 59) past North Creek Campground. The uphill trailhead leaves Sunset Fields at milepost 78.4 on the Blue Ridge Parkway and winds down Apple Orchard Mountain, generally following the headwaters of North Creek. Hikers will follow the coursing stream as it travels down the mountain. The trail pauses at a wooden platform overlooking the waterfalls then travels to a boardwalk at the base of the waterfall. Hikers stopping at the middle trailhead quickly encounter wooden bridges criss-crossing the creek as they progress uphill to the viewing platform. The most downhill trailhead begins in relatively flatter terrain before eventually ascending a steeper grade toward the viewing platform.

properties.name: BELFAST
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Use the Belfast Trailhead to access #9 Belfast Trail to Devils Marbleyard, James River Face Wilderness, and the A.T. Parking is available for approximately five compact cars. There is more room for parking a short distance along the road to the left.

properties.name: SULPHUR SPRINGS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Use the Suplhur Springs Trailhead to access #3001 Sulphur Srping Trail In the gravel parking lot, there's room for two or three compact cars.

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Use the Petites Gap A.T. Trailhead to access #1 A.T. and #3004 Glenwood Horse along #35 Petities Gap Road between Thunder Ridge Wilderness and James River Face Wilderness. There is room for approximately 6 vehicles in the gravel parking lot.

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

properties.description: The North Creek Road (FSR #59) Trailhead serves #17 Apple Orchard Falls Trail & #18 Cornelius Creek Trail Four trailheads exist for the Apple Orchard Falls National Recreation Trail: one at the top, off the Blue Ridge Parkway; two trailheads in the middle of the trail, off Apple Tree Road (FSR3034) and Parkers Gap Road (812) respectively; and one trailhead at the downhill end, at the end of North Creek Road (FSR 59) past North Creek Campground. properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

properties.description: The Parkers Gap Road (FSR #812) Trailhead serves #17A Apple Orchard Spur Four trailheads exist for the Apple Orchard Falls National Recreation Trail: one at the top, off the Blue Ridge Parkway; two trailheads in the middle of the trail, off Apple Tree Road (FSR3034) and Parkers Gap Road (812) respectively; and one trailhead at the downhill end, at the end of North Creek Road (FSR 59) past North Creek Campground. properties.name: PICKETT SPRINGS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is a trailhead for NFST #403 Sherman Gap Trial located on Fort Valley Road just south of Elizabeth Furnace Campground.

properties.name: COBBLER MOUTAIN
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Use Cobbler Mountain Trailhead to access trails #611 - Cobbler Mountain and #611.1 - Cobbler Mountain Access

properties.name: HIDDEN VALLEY
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: With vast fields of wildflowers that attract countless butterflies, birds, and other wildlife, the Hidden Valley Recreation Area is appropriately named due to its secluded and hidden feeling. Ample equestian, hiker, and angler parking for access to the Jacskon River's stocked trout waters and access to trails #481 - Hidden Valley Trail, #481D - Jackson River Gorge Trail, #610 - Hidden Valley West and other trails in the area. Nearby lodging includes an antebellum-era mansion which is now run as a Bed and Breakfast and camping at the Hidden Valley Campground.

properties.name: BOLAR MOUNTAIN
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Bolar Mountain Recreation Area at Lake Moomaw offers visitors a fun getaway on Lake Moomaw. The area provides opportunities for plenty of activities, including camping, boating, fishing and hiking, as well as volleyball and a playground. The recreation area sits on the northern end of Lake Moomaw, a manmade lake covering 2,530 acres along the Jackson River. The lake's average depth is 80 feet and it has 43 miles of wooded shoreline. Bolar Mountain boasts 11 miles of hiking trails that lead to two impressive scenic overlooks: Islands Overlook Spur and Grouse Point Overlook.

properties.name: ELIZABETH FURNACE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: Use this trailhead to access trails in the Elizabeth Furnace Area including #463 - Botts, #405.1 - Tuscarora-Veach Gap, #483 - Pig Iron Intepretive, and #483A - Charcoal Interpretive
